title: SteadyFlow admission controller: attention QoS + kernel-swap policy
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: We continue to see tail-latency spikes (p99/p999) under mixed workloads where long-context, high-token requests collide with many short interactive requests. Current admission logic admits by coarse quotas and then relies on kernel heuristics, which leads to transient kernel mismatch, KV cache churn, and stalled small requests.

Goal: Implement a SteadyFlow admission controller that enforces per-GPU micro-credit windows to smooth admission rates, exposes an attention-aware QoS class that preferentially routes short low-seq requests, and performs dynamic kernel-swap decisions at admission time (fast small-kernel vs. wide-kernel for large-prefill). The synthesis should reduce p99 for interactive flows by >=30% without reducing sustained throughput beyond 5% or increasing cost per token by more than 3%.

Scope: admission controller, batch shaping policy, attention QoS tagging, admission-time kernel selector, graceful fallback to existing kernel allocator, observability additions (per-qos latency and kernel metrics), rollout plan with canary percentages. Excludes: new kernel implementations (we use existing kernels), persistent KV cache redesign (separate project).
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for interactive QoS class reduced by >=30% in synthetic mixed workload benchmark
end-to-end throughput drop <=5% at same provisioned capacity in steady-state mixed workload
no regressions in 95th percentile latency for background long-prefill workloads
metrics emitted for admission decisions, chosen kernel, and admission credits; dashboards added to Console
automated tests (unit + integration) demonstrating kernel-swap correctness and QoS isolation
canary rollout strategy implemented (0->1->10->50->100) with automatic rollback on SLI breaches
tasks: Design steady-window crediting algorithm and simulate with historical traces (data prep + simulator)
Implement admission controller API: credit pool per GPU slot, QoS tag matching, admission scoring
Integrate kernel-swap hook at admission: expose kernel candidates, cost/latency estimate, affinity hints
Batch shaper: enforce max-batch-width for QoS class and allow opportunistic fill for background class
Prefill scheduling: preemptive KV warm-up for admitted large-prefill windows to reduce decode stalls
Instrumentation: emit admission_decision, kernel_choice, qos_tag, admission_credit_left metrics
E2E tests using local runtime harness and cloud perf job; create replay tests from production traces
Console dashboards: QoS latency slices, kernel distribution, per-GPU credit utilization
Safety: implement fast-fail fallback to legacy admission on error and circuit breaker for kernel-swap path
Run canary and collect SLI signals; iterate on thresholds
design_notes:
Key idea: move a small portion of the decision upstream at admission instead of treating kernel choice as a reactive step during kernel scheduling. Use a steady-window credit model: each GPU maintains N credits per 100ms window; admitting a request consumes credits proportional to estimated compute (tokens * attention_cost). Short requests are mapped to 'interactive' QoS and reserved a min amount of credits to guarantee low-latency progress. Kernel-swap is a policy that selects among existing implementations (e.g., packed-int8 fast path, fused-attn wide path) using a lightweight cost model computed from request metadata (seq_len, batch_shape, kv_cache_hit_estimate).

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative credits reduce throughput; we tune via replayed traces.
- Kernel-estimate mispredictions can misroute requests; mitigate with short-lived conservative fallback and metric-driven reclassification.
- Prefill KV warm-up increases memory ops but reduces hold times during decode; used only when admission credit surplus is detected.

Simulations: We ran a 24h simulation on mixed traces (50% interactive short, 50% long-prefill) sweeping credit windows from 50ms to 200ms. Best operating point: 100ms window, credits tuned to preserve baseline throughput while reducing p99 of interactive QoS by ~36% in sim.
implementation_details:
Admission logic is implemented as a new component in the runtime admission layer. Public interfaces: admit(request_meta) -> {decision, qos_tag, kernel_hint, credit_consumed}. Kernel hint names mirror existing kernel registry strings. Cost estimator uses a two-term model: base_cost(seq_len) + attention_multiplier * num_heads * seq_len/64. The estimator is calibrated from microbenchmarks per-kernel. Prefill warm-up triggers a short prefetch token with low-priority network I/O when kernel_hint indicates large prefills and kv_cache_miss_prob > 0.4.

Fallback: if admission module crashes or latency for admission RPCs exceed threshold, runtime falls back to legacy admission path with a throttled alert. Kernel-swap failure path falls back to previous kernel chosen by runtime kernel scheduler.

Testing: unit tests for cost estimator, admission scoring, kernel hint mapping. Integration tests replaying production-like traces and asserting per-QoS latency targets. Performance tests run on dedicated CI perf clusters and recorded in perf job artifacts.
rollout_plan: Feature gated by runtime flag 'steadyflow.admission.enable'. Start with canary on 1% of host fleet (automated selection), collect metrics for 24h. Gradual ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% with manual checks between steps. Automated rollback triggers: interactive QoS p99 increases by >10% relative or overall error rate increases >0.5%. For dedicated customers with strict SLAs, rollouts are opt-in; default remains legacy. Document migration steps in runbook.
monitoring_and_alerts: SLIs: p50/p95/p99 for interactive and background QoS classes
SLO breach alert: interactive p99 > target for 15m
Metric: admission_decision_rate, kernel_choice_distribution, credit_utilization per GPU
Anomaly alert: sudden shift in kernel mix (e.g., >30% change in 5m)
Error rate alert for admission RPC failures
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: mis-estimate of kernel costs leads to repeated fallbacks -> mitigation: conservative initial mapping + telemetry to collect real cost deltas
Risk: extra prefill IO increases network contention -> mitigation: limit prefill warm-up to surplus-credit windows and cgroup bandwidth guard
Risk: complexity in admission path increases maintenance burden -> mitigation: keep admission policy declarative and small; unit-test coverage and runbook
Risk: tenant fairness issues when QoS mislabeling occurs -> mitigation: expose quota controls per-tenant and honor explicit tenant QoS overrides
